objective: Forge a signature that verifies for an attacker-chosen message
assumptions: The attacker can submit a signature to a verify() call on 1.4.2.
expectedWork: Trivial: one crafted 64-byte value, no key material needed.
uncertainty: None within the tested entry point. Fixed in 1.4.3 (runs #11, #14).

objective: Characterise which out-of-range signatures are accepted
method: Seeded sample of 2000 out-of-range (r, s) pairs against a valid message.
assumptions: The sampled classes {0, n, n+1, 2n, 2^256-1} are representative of out-of-range inputs an attacker would try.
expectedWork: 63 of 2000 sampled pairs accepted, all with r = 0; 0 accepted on 1.4.3 (run #14).

objective: Recover the private key from the public key
method: Generic elliptic-curve discrete logarithm (Pollard rho class).
source: Standard analysis (sample statement, not measured in this project)
assumptions: No implementation weakness beyond those tested.
Attacker has the public key only.
Nonces are generated correctly (not tested here).
expectedWork: About 2^128 group operations; infeasible with known classical hardware.
uncertainty: Textbook estimate. This project measured nothing about it and does not test nonce generation.

objective: Recover the private key with a fault-tolerant quantum computer
source: Published literature (sample summary; no specific figure adopted)
assumptions: A fault-tolerant machine of sufficient size exists, which none does today.
expectedWork: Published resource estimates vary by orders of magnitude with architecture and error-correction assumptions; this project adopts no single figure.
uncertainty: High. Relevance depends on Acme's data-lifetime requirements, which were not part of intake.

objective: Extract the private key through timing side channels
method: Statistical timing analysis of sign() with chosen inputs.
uncertainty: No timing or power measurement was performed; the side-channel test is unsupported in the sandbox (task-010 blocked).
